people.gloss: The purple of the evening hills (Vương Bột: yên quang ngưng nhi mộ sơn tử)
people.role: Head of Yên Quang Các since 1150; moved it to the wild mulberry wood in 1187; Lạc Hà's pill supplier
people.appearance: A lean, unhurried man in a smoke-grey robe with his sleeves tied, whose lips are stained faintly purple from seventy years of tasting pills.
people.backstory: Tào Mộ Tử was left at the pavilion's steppe gate as a newborn in 1080, in the hour of the evening glow. The founder Vi Ngưng Yên (vi_ngung_yen) named him from the line the pavilion was named for, the purple of the evening hills. He is the one inner disciple without an herb name. He grew up among the furnaces and, by the pavilion's rule, tasted every pill he made. When Vi died in her breakthrough in 1150 (N-yen_quang-02), her Dao partner Diêm Tử Tô (diem_tu_to) refused the headship and would not light a furnace again. The pavilion made Tào head at seventy, a Trúc Cơ over a Kết Đan grand elder. After Lạc Hà moved its seat up the mountain in 1185, its Maple Hall under Chử Hồng Diệp (chu_hong_diep) began making the sect's own pills. Tào saw his best customer learning to grow its own. In 1187 he moved the furnaces and beds to the wild mulberry wood beside Tang Ma Thành and kept the steppe as the Dusk Field (N-yen_quang-03). In 1195 he made the veil and tincture with which Lạc Hà's Hình Lạc Nhạn (hinh_lac_nhan) walked into the miasma.
people.wants: To make the miasma antidote, the one pill the Maple Hall cannot make, before his lord stops needing the pavilion at all.
people.secret: He knows what Hình Lạc Nhạn's tincture is for. The strength she asked for in 1197 is enough for a thousand paces of the grey, not three hundred. He made it and took his fee in miasma-root from the grey's edge, which he needs for the antidote. He has told no one, least of all Cảnh Trường Thiên, who has forbidden her the plain. Since the winter he has been testing the antidote on himself, a dose a week, and he has kept Khổng Ích Mẫu (khong_ich_mau) home from the Watch this year to write down every dose and every fit, so that if it kills him the next maker knows where to stop.

people.role: Grand elder and co-founder (1065); keeps the Dusk Field at the old seat and has not lit a furnace since 1150
people.appearance: A tall old man with a perilla leaf pinned to his collar, who sits beside a cold bronze furnace on the steppe every evening and polishes it until the light goes.
people.backstory: Diêm Tử Tô was born in 1000 in Sơn Trà Thôn, a camellia-picker's son, and came to Lạc Hà's outer gate with Wood enough for any sect and just enough Earth for its inner one. There he met Vi Ngưng Yên (vi_ngung_yen), the gate's best herbalist. In 1065, with their lord's leave, the two of them founded the pavilion on the steppe below Lạc Hà's seat to make its pills (V107). He lit its first furnace and wrote the furnace art it still teaches. In 1150 he made the pill for Vi's breakthrough to Nguyên Anh. She died in it (N-yen_quang-02). He refused the headship, gave it to Vi's foundling Tào Mộ Tử (tao_mo_tu), and has not lit a furnace since. When the pavilion moved to the mulberry wood in 1187 he stayed on the steppe, where she is buried. He keeps the Dusk Field with Văn Đương Quy (van_duong_quy) and teaches anyone who walks out at sunset.
people.wants: To light a furnace once more before he dies, for Văn Đương Quy's Kết Đan, and to know why Vi changed the recipe.
people.secret: Sorting her notes for the move in 1187, he found that Vi changed the recipe of her breakthrough pill the night before. She added a dusk herb she had bought at Lạc Đan Thanh's stall in Vật Hoa Thị (A186), because the drought had thinned the bed grown from Hàn Thanh Cao's seed. He does not know whether Lạc sold her a bad herb or whether she asked him for one. He has never asked, because either answer would end something. This spring Lạc sent word that he will tell, for one pill brewed in the Cold Furnace, and Chử Hồng Diệp's (chu_hong_diep) letter came the same month with a recipe very like Vi's.

people.role: The pavilion's best picker; keeps the Dusk Field with the grand elder
people.appearance: A brown, wiry woman in a straw cape, always kneeling, with a gourd at her hip and grass seeds in her hair.
people.backstory: A girl from Hoa Khê Thôn, where lovers drop their names into the brook (A194). She took the herb name Đương Quy, 'ought to return', and has picked on the steppe at sunset for seventy years. When the furnaces moved in 1187 she stayed on the Dusk Field with Diêm Tử Tô (diem_tu_to). At ninety she is ready for Kết Đan. She will take a pill from no one but Diêm, and he will not light a furnace.
people.wants: To pick one sunset on the steppe without being asked a question, and to see the dusk-wormwood seed itself.
people.secret: Each dusk she wraps a pinch of the Dusk Field's best evening herb for a Tang Ma Thành mother whose son is wasting, and Tiền Tiểu Đồng (tien_tieu_dong) carries it into the city for her for nothing.

people.role: Keeper of the furnaces at the mulberry wood

people.backstory: A charcoal-burner's son from Thán Ổ Thôn who keeps the new seat's furnaces and burns their charcoal from mulberry deadwood; Diêm Tử Tô (diem_tu_to) taught him, and Tào Mộ Tử works him harder. He draws the dawn-bank lots from a bag with the short sticks sewn into the lining, and Mộ Ngưu Tất (mo_nguu_tat) has banked the founder's coals eleven days running.

people.role: Keeper of the mulberry wood; sells the pavilion's pills
people.appearance: A sharp-faced woman in a silk robe dyed the green of mulberry leaves, with a price list sewn inside her sleeve.
people.backstory: A Tang Ma Thành silk-dealer's daughter. She took the herb name Tang Ký in 1160 when she found mistletoe on the wild mulberries three tiles from her father's shop. It was she who told Tào Mộ Tử (tao_mo_tu) the wood was there. She keeps it now and sells the pavilion's pills in Tang Ma and to Lạc Hà. Since Lạc Hà's Maple Hall began selling against the pavilion, she has sold crates of its pills to a Thúy Vi buyer in Tang Ma Thành under Lạc Hà's posted price, and she fills them by cutting the wound salve the pavilion sells the city's rope-walkers.
people.wants: A bench among the Thúy Vi guild's elders, as one of them and not as a supplier.
people.secret: She is grafting wild mistletoe in a locked shed to sell the pavilion's rarest herb as her own stock; Cố Tằm Nhi (co_tam_nhi) is paid to water it and told it is for the head.

people.role: Outer disciple placed from Lạc Hà
people.appearance: A habit of tilting her head at every kind word, as though checking it for a flaw.
people.backstory: She failed Lạc Hà's dusk test three times and asked to be placed here, because the Dusk Field works the same hour. Tô Bình Chu (to_binh_chu) placed her in 1199, and Lạc Hà takes its tenth until 1229. Her first bed of dusk-wormwood drowned in the spring's first rain, and her sandals went down the stream the same week.

people.backstory: A river-mouth girl from Thủy Khẩu Thôn and Lạc Hà's best inner-gate herbalist. In 1065, with her lord's leave and her Dao partner Diêm Tử Tô (diem_tu_to), she founded the pavilion on the steppe below Lạc Hà's seat to make its pills (V107). In 1080 she found a newborn at the gate in the evening light and named him Tào Mộ Tử (tao_mo_tu). She died in 1150 in her breakthrough to Nguyên Anh (N-yen_quang-02).
